statement: For F_m(u,v,y)=(-1)^(u dot v)-(1-y)1{u=v=0}, Delta_y(F_m)/I_y(F_m) >= log_2((2^m-1)^2+1); hence no universal bound Delta_i(f)<=C I_i(f) can hold for every Boolean f and every coordinate i.
assumptions: uniform measure on {0,1}^{2m} times selector y in {-1,1}
proof_or_counterexample: Independent Walsh derivation gives Bhat(alpha,beta)=2^-m(-1)^(alpha dot beta), dhat=2^-2m, I_y=2^-2m. Entropy identity gives Delta_y=sum_T r_T[h_2(b_T^2/r_T)+J(2a_Tb_T/r_T)] >= I_y log_2((2^m-1)^2+1). Direct truth-table run: python -X utf8 test_selector.py, m=1,2,3 ratios 4.867668747, 8.030013847, 10.255970235; each exceeded its lower bound; total influences matched m+(2m+1)/2^(2m).
remaining_gap: This refutes only the all-coordinate induction input. A suitable-coordinate or amortized lemma is still unproved; it does not settle FEI.
status: independently checked proof of intermediate counterexample

statement: A universal existence-of-good-coordinate bound Delta_i(f)<=K Inf_i(f) for each nonconstant Boolean f implies FEI with the same K.
assumptions: The existence-of-coordinate inequality is assumed at every dimension and every restriction
source_quote: If there exists one finite universal K such that every nonconstant Boolean f has a coordinate i with Delta_i(f)<=K Inf_i(f), then FEI holds with the same K.
proof_or_counterexample: Induction on dimension: H(f)=Delta_i+average H(f_i^+/-), I(f)=Inf_i+average I(f_i^+/-); restrictions have fewer relevant variables; constant base case is zero.
remaining_gap: The assumed coordinate-selection inequality is unproved; source identifies this type of induction as conditional.

statement: For w504's quadratic selector family F_m with even m>=2, each base coordinate j has Inf_j=1/2+2^-m and Delta_j<=2-(m/2)2^-m<4 Inf_j.
assumptions: exact F_m in w504 PROOF.md section 3
proof_or_counterexample: Independently derived the restriction spectra: fixing b_j=1 leaves a bent core with entropy m-2; fixing b_j=0 leaves a one-point flip with zero-control coefficients 2a epsilon-2t and three blocks -2t. Their entropies give Delta_j=2-(m/2)t+[L(1,2a)-2L(1,a)]/2. The bracket equals -[R(1-a)+R(1+a)]<=0 because R(u)=u^2 log_2 u is convex on [1/2,3/2]. Independent truth-table run python -X utf8 test_w504.py passed m=2,4,6,8.
remaining_gap: Only this explicit family is covered; arbitrary restrictions are not shown to preserve it, and no universal coordinate rule follows.
status: independently checked proof of special family

The Fourier selector-present slice has mass t and each slice at most 2^m indices; entropy chain rule gives H<=m+h_2(t). With t=2^-m, h_2(t)<=mt+t/ln 2 and m>=2, this is <=2I. statement: For any Boolean f and coordinate i, 0<=Delta_i(f)<=h_2(q)+4q(1-q), q=Inf_i(f).
proof_or_counterexample: From the exact identity, Jensen gives sum r h_2(w)<=h_2(q); J(t)<=t^2<=4w(1-w), and Jensen on w(1-w) gives sum r J(t)<=4q(1-q). J(t)<=t^2 follows from its positive even-power series whose coefficients sum to J(1)=1.
remaining_gap: h_2(q)/q diverges as q tends to zero; prior owner memory records a sharper high-influence reduction, so no novelty is asserted.
status: independently checked proof of elementary bound

statement: For an arbitrary law p on subsets S of [n], H_2(p)<=sum_i h_2(q_i), where q_i=P(i in S); this fact alone cannot yield H_2(p)<=C sum_i q_i with universal C.
proof_or_counterexample: Entropy chain rule and conditioning give subadditivity. For n=1, P(S={1})=q and P(S=empty)=1-q gives H/I=h_2(q)/q>=log_2(1/q), unbounded as q tends to zero. The prior P0162 attempt card also records an n-singleton law obstruction and the Boolean f^2=1 constraint.
remaining_gap: General probability laws need not be Boolean Fourier spectra; Boolean convolution identities are required for FEI.
status: independently checked proof for arbitrary laws

statement: w505's exact identity Delta_i=sum_T r_T[h_2(w_T)+J(t_T)] and nonnegative lower bound by sum_T b_T^2 log_2(r_T/b_T^2) hold for Boolean uniform-cube f.
proof_or_counterexample: Expanding phi(x)=x log_2(1/x) on each Fourier pair gives the equality; J(t)=1-h_2((1+t)/2)>=0. The binary entropy term r h_2(w) includes b^2 log_2(r/b^2), with a further nonnegative term. Zero r contributes zero.
remaining_gap: The identity has no universal upper bound by a single coordinate influence; the suitable-coordinate lemma remains unproved.

statement: w505's bent-point selector family F_m has H_2(F_m)<=2I(F_m) for every m>=1.
source_quote: The complete H/I ratio therefore does not grow like the defective Delta_y/I_y ratio.
proof_or_counterexample: The selector-present spectral slice has mass rho=2^-2m; conditional on selector presence or absence, at most 2^(2m) base Fourier indices occur. Thus H<=2m+h_2(rho). Direct flips give I=m+(2m+1)rho; h_2(rho)<=2m rho+rho/ln2 yields H<=2I. Independent truth tables m=1,2,3 corroborated.
remaining_gap: Only this family is covered, and FEI for every Boolean function is unproved.
status: independently checked proof of special family

assumptions: the small-influence coordinate premise is assumed, not proved
source_quote: From section 1 and 0<=h_2<=1, every coordinate has 0<=Delta_i(f)<=2.

remaining_gap: At tau=1/16, existence of K_0 for all Boolean f with every influence <1/16 remains unproved. Prior owner F4 work has a sharper related reduction; no novelty claim.
